scenes.headline: How to read a middle layer with a derivative
scenes.sub: The Jacobian lens: carry an activation to the final layer, then decode it.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Yoyo! What is a middle layer of a language model about to say? The Jacobian lens answers with a derivative.

scenes.text: Carry a middle-layer activation into the final layer's basis with the corpus-averaged Jacobian, then decode it with the model's own unembedding.
scenes.say: Carry a middle-layer activation into the final layer's basis with the averaged Jacobian. Then decode it with the model's own unembedding.

scenes.title: A lens is a choice of transport

left.title: Logit lens
items: Assumes one basis for every layer
left.say: The logit lens unembeds a middle layer directly. But each layer rewrites the basis, so the coordinates don't line up.

right.title: Jacobian lens
items: Transport through the layers above first
The transport is the averaged derivative
Readable content in the middle of the stack
right.say: The Jacobian lens first maps it through the layers above, using their derivative. That works mid-stack, where the interesting computation lives.

steps.say: Pick a middle-layer activation. Running every layer above would be exact, but nonlinear, and no longer a lens.
So multiply by one matrix, J: the derivative of the final layer with respect to this one.
Unembed and rank. At the nose of an ASCII-art face, middle layers read out nose, a word absent from the prompt.

items.say: Run a corpus through: a thousand sequences of a hundred twenty-eight tokens.
Backpropagate from the final layer, summing each position's influence on itself and every later position.
Average over positions and prompts: one tangent, taken at the corpus average, used for everything.

scenes.title: Top-5 concept-swap success, paper-reported
scenes.note: the J-space part holds a median of only 6–7% of the variance
scenes.say: Do the directions matter causally? Swapping along a concept's J-space part succeeds fifty-nine percent of the time, though it holds only six to seven percent of the variance.

scenes.text: The lens is a tangent: a first-order, on-average picture of what a layer is disposed to say, not a replay.
scenes.say: The lens is a tangent: what a layer is disposed to say, to first order and on average. Not a replay.

recap: Transport with the averaged Jacobian, then unembed
It reads content the output has moved past
A small J-space part drives concept swaps
scenes.say: To recap: transport with a derivative, unembed, and read what the middle is about to say.
